items.title: THE THRESHOLD
items.caption: The one public page of the old site: a starfield being drawn very slowly toward the centre, and two unmarked doors. Nothing behind either is named. The left one is sealed and the right one records you on the way in.
items.shot: 1600×1000, four seconds after load, no interaction.

items.title: THE THRESHOLD
items.caption: The pull. 260 stars falling inward at 0.55% of the frame per tick, which is the whole animation.
items.shot: 1600×1000, four seconds after load, no interaction.

items.title: THE GRAVITY WELL
items.caption: PHASE 00. The wordmark is not type — it is a particle cluster holding the shape of one, and it comes apart if you grab it. Click is a shockwave, hold is a vortex. The four colour families are the whole SLIME palette: slime, mint, purple, hot pink.
items.shot: 1600×1000, six seconds after load, cluster left alone.

items.title: THE GRAVITY WELL
items.caption: The cluster running untouched. Nothing here is a video loop or a shader — it is a CPU particle simulation being asked to hold a word.
items.shot: 1600×1000, six seconds after load, cluster left alone.

items.title: THE VOID CONSOLE
items.caption: PHASE 01, the index of the whole old site in five numbered sections. This is the page that says 37 INSTRUMENTS · 3 CHAPELS out loud, and it is the manifest the rack at /leviathan was rebuilt from.
items.shot: 1600×1000, after ENTER THE VOID, four and a half seconds to settle.

items.title: THE VOID CONSOLE
items.caption: The descent through all five sections — 01 THE CORPUS, 02 THE WIKI, 03 ANNIE, 04 THE TEMPLE, 05 OPEN A CHANNEL.
items.shot: 1600×1000, after ENTER THE VOID, four and a half seconds to settle.

items.title: THE SINGULARITY
items.caption: The second wing’s door. Three checks stand behind it and the first two log who you are before the third tells you whether you are getting in — an ordering the page states plainly rather than hides.
items.shot: 1600×1000, four and a half seconds after load.

items.title: THE TEMPLE
items.caption: The section index for the chapels — the three standalone instruments that sit outside the console.
items.shot: 1600×1000, four and a half seconds after load.

items.title: CHAPEL III · THE CLOCK
items.caption: Eleven years of one person’s messages as a single spiral. Angle is the hour of the day, radius is the date — first message at the centre, last at the rim. Nothing is excluded, weighted or smoothed. The dark wedge is sleep.
items.shot: 1600×1400, nine seconds after load — the spiral draws itself in and this is where it stops.

items.title: CHAPEL III · THE CLOCK
items.caption: The spiral drawing itself, 68,998 points, from the first message outward.
items.shot: 1600×1400, nine seconds after load — the spiral draws itself in and this is where it stops.

items.title: CHAPEL II · THE VOICE
items.caption: A trigram chain over one half of the corpus. It is not her, not a quote and not a prediction — it is the shape of 434,795 words with the meaning taken out, which is a thing worth being able to look at once.

items.title: CHAPEL I · THE ORACLE
items.caption: The seeded oracle. A field, a deterministic random number generator and a sigil — the same question returns the same answer forever, which is the joke and also the method.

items.title: THE LINE
items.caption: The family tree as an hourglass around one focus person: ancestors climbing away above, descendants spreading below, spouses beside. 515 people, 218 families, 15 generations, 1575→2002, and it says out loud that 71% of it is sourced.
items.shot: 1600×1000, seven seconds after load, at the default focus.

items.title: THE LINE
items.caption: Re-centring. Click anyone and the whole hourglass re-lays itself around them — this is four generations being walked in one take.
items.shot: 1600×1000, seven seconds after load, at the default focus.

items.title: THE LINE · THE INDEX
items.caption: The same dataset with the drawing taken away: every person in the tree as a row, sourced or not.

items.title: THE WIKI
items.caption: The prose reader — 486 pages, nine domains, the whole second brain with the instruments deliberately left off it. The room at /brain is this rebuilt; this is what it looked like first.
items.shot: 1600×1000, seven seconds after load, at the index.

items.title: THE TRANSCRIPT
items.caption: The old reader for the message record — the same 134,348 messages now at /transcript, back when getting to the first line meant downloading all 9.4 MB of them.
items.shot: 1600×1000, nine seconds after load — most of which is the envelope arriving.

items.title: THE HUB
items.caption: The whole site folded down to a phone. The console does not fit on one and never pretended to, so the small screen got its own front door instead.
